aggressive_definition_excerpt: Alcohol intake was more strongly related with localized than with advanced prostate tumors.
study_design: Prospective cohort study analyzed using a case-cohort approach
reason: The prospective study analyzes incident primary prostate cancer overall and also reports an exposure association by localized versus advanced tumor status. The analytic case-cohort sample size is not reported; 58,279 is the baseline source cohort size.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Increased associations were found for alcohol from white wine and fortified wines compared to nondrinkers, but not for red wine. The RRs (95% CI) in the intake category of > or = 15 g/day were 3.3 (1.2-9.2) and 2.3 (1.2-4.7), respectively, after additional adjustment for total alcohol intake.
estimate_classifications.reason: The numeric white-wine estimate is for prostate cancer risk overall and is not identified as an advanced-tumor estimate.

additional_estimates.comparison: Alcohol intake; exposure contrast not specified
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Alcohol intake was more strongly related with localized than with advanced prostate tumors.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
